# 1 Introduction

## What Is Mathematics?

Mathematics (from Greek μάθημα máthēma , "knowledge", "study") is an area of study involving concepts such as quantity, structure, space, change, order, logic, pattern recognition, measurement, model building, and proof . Mathematicians seek out patterns,[2][3] formulate new conjectures, and establish truth by rigorous deduction from appropriately chosen axioms and definitions.[4]

This process of discovery and justification may come through deductive reasoning or induction .

In practice, mathematical proofs vary widely depending on their subject matter; some subjects have more precise standards than others. In mathematics education, written arguments are often called 'proofs' regardless of strength. For example, a statistical hypothesis test might involve steps whose correctness cannot reasonably be doubted but which do not constitute formal mathematical proof within any strict sense of those words.

The word "mathematical" comes from Ancient Greece where there was no concept of modern-day disciplines like philosophy or science. Instead, all areas were considered part of one discipline: episteme ("science"). In 1890, a French mathematician named Gaston Julia posed this question: "Suppose that you have two eggs. One is an ordinary hen's egg; one has been fertilized by a rooster.

The following is a reprint of an article written in 1960 and published as "Two Little Words" (in which I was not involved) on page 4 of the February issue of American Weekly magazine:
It's been said before but it bears repeating: There are two things you should never do with your children; tell them they're stupid or try to make them perfect. If we want our young people to grow up into responsible adults who will be able to cope successfully with life itself--and there isn't any other kind worth having --we must teach them how to think for themselves instead of just what to think . We have got to give them some tools so when their teachers say something like this :
"The United States has no right to exist."
or even worse,
"We don't need science because God made us all He needed"
they won't automatically accept these statements without question .
We've had too many generations brought up under such conditions where everything from religion down through history books were taught only one way , always presented as if it were true whether it actually happened or not! And then those same kids went out into society expecting everyone else would agree with them!
But now more than ever before parents face new problems : How much freedom shall my child enjoy? What about his education ? Should he go to college at public expense?
And most important of all today, HOW CAN WE TEACH OUR CHILDREN TO THINK FOR THEMSELVES ?
I believe the answer lies within ourselves ; each parent needs first to find answers to questions like these:
What did YOU learn while growing up?
How well does YOUR present knowledge fit together with yours?
Do you know enough yourself to help others understand better why certain ideas seem wrong?
If you answered yes to ALL three above questions, congratulations ! You already possess the basic tool necessary to pass along to future generations the ability to reason correctly !
Now let me ask another set of questions:
Did anyone EVER explain WHY evolution works?
Why doesn't man die after eating meat?
Is gravity really stronger near Earth 's surface?
Can anything move faster than light?
Are atoms real objects or merely patterns of energy?
Does time flow forward or backward?
Have scientists discovered every element yet known?
Will nuclear power destroy civilization forever?
These aren't easy questions to answer ... nor are they simple ones either... But once learned properly, they become part of everyday living rather than mere facts stored away somewhere inside your head until called upon occasionally during exams.

"We don't need science because God made us all He needed"
they won't automatically accept these statements without question .
We've had too many generations brought up under such conditions where everything from religion down through history books were taught only one way , always presented as if it were true whether it actually happened or not! And then those same kids went out into society expecting everyone else would agree with them!
But now more than ever before parents face new problems : How much freedom shall my child enjoy? What about his education ? Should he go to college at public expense?
And most important of all today, HOW CAN WE TEACH OUR CHILDREN TO THINK FOR THEMSELVES ?
I believe the answer lies within ourselves ; each parent needs first to find answers to questions like these:
What did YOU learn while growing up?
How well does YOUR present knowledge fit together with yours?
Do you know enough yourself to help others understand better why certain ideas seem wrong?
If you answered yes to ALL three above questions, congratulations ! You already possess the basic tool necessary to pass along to future generations the ability to reason correctly !
Now let me ask another set of questions:
Did anyone EVER explain WHY evolution works?
Why doesn't man die after eating meat?
Is gravity really stronger near Earth 's surface?
Can anything move faster than light?
Are atoms real objects or merely patterns of energy?
Does time flow forward or backward?
Have scientists discovered every element yet known?
Will nuclear power destroy civilization forever?
These aren't easy questions to answer ... nor are they simple ones either... But once learned properly, they become part of everyday living rather than mere facts stored away somewhere inside your head until called upon occasionally during exams.

Two cats are sitting together on their owner's lap when they notice that there isn't enough room for both of them to be comfortable so they decide to switch places:
